   118	    private func fill(_ rep: NSBitmapImageRep, r: UInt8, g: UInt8, b: UInt8) {
   119	        guard let bytes = rep.bitmapData else {
   120	            XCTFail("bitmapData nil")
   121	            return
   122	        }
   123	        let spp = rep.samplesPerPixel
   124	        let bpr = rep.bytesPerRow
   125	        for y in 0..<rep.pixelsHigh {
   126	            for x in 0..<rep.pixelsWide {
   127	                let o = y * bpr + x * spp
   128	                bytes[o] = r
   129	                bytes[o + 1] = g
   130	                bytes[o + 2] = b
   131	                if spp >= 4 { bytes[o + 3] = 255 }
   132	            }
   133	        }
   134	    }

   136	    /// Count coarse-grid samples inside `rect` that are not near-white.
   137	    private func countNonWhiteInRegion(_ rep: NSBitmapImageRep, rect: NSRect) -> Int {
   138	        let spp = rep.samplesPerPixel
   139	        let bpr = rep.bytesPerRow
   140	        guard let bytes = rep.bitmapData, spp >= 3, bpr > 0 else { return 0 }
   141	        let x0 = max(0, Int(rect.minX.rounded(.down)))
   142	        let y0 = max(0, Int(rect.minY.rounded(.down)))
   143	        let x1 = min(rep.pixelsWide, Int(rect.maxX.rounded(.up)))
   144	        let y1 = min(rep.pixelsHigh, Int(rect.maxY.rounded(.up)))
   145	        guard x1 > x0, y1 > y0 else { return 0 }
   146	        let step = max(1, min(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) / 16)
   147	        var count = 0
   148	        for y in stride(from: y0, to: y1, by: step) {
   149	            for x in stride(from: x0, to: x1, by: step) {
   150	                let o = y * bpr + x * spp
   151	                let r = bytes[o]
   152	                let g = bytes[o + 1]
   153	                let b = bytes[o + 2]
   154	                // Near-white threshold mirrors sampleNonBlankPixels (~0.92).
   155	                if r < 235 || g < 235 || b < 235 {
   156	                    count += 1
   157	                }
   158	            }
   159	        }
   160	        return count
   161	    }

     5	/// Bounded restart policy for an app-managed engine. The schedule is indexed
     6	/// from one, and stays at its final value when callers allow more attempts
     7	/// than explicit delays. Keeping this policy separate from process launching
     8	/// makes the operational limits straightforward to test and tune.
     9	struct EngineRestartPolicy: Equatable, Sendable {
    10	    static let `default` = EngineRestartPolicy(
    11	        backoffSchedule: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30],
    12	        maximumAttempts: 6,
    13	        pollInterval: 1,
    14	        healthyResetInterval: 60,
    15	        consecutiveFailureThreshold: 3
    16	    )
    17	
    18	    let backoffSchedule: [TimeInterval]
    19	    let maximumAttempts: Int
    20	    let pollInterval: TimeInterval
    21	    let healthyResetInterval: TimeInterval
    22	    let consecutiveFailureThreshold: Int
    23	
    24	    init(
    25	        backoffSchedule: [TimeInterval],
    26	        maximumAttempts: Int,
    27	        pollInterval: TimeInterval = Self.default.pollInterval,
    28	        healthyResetInterval: TimeInterval = Self.default.healthyResetInterval,
    29	        consecutiveFailureThreshold: Int = Self.default.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    30	    ) {
    31	        self.backoffSchedule = backoffSchedule.isEmpty ? Self.default.backoffSchedule : backoffSchedule
    32	        self.maximumAttempts = max(1, maximumAttempts)
    33	        self.pollInterval = max(0.1, pollInterval)
    34	        self.healthyResetInterval = max(0, healthyResetInterval)
    35	        self.consecutiveFailureThreshold = max(1, consecutiveFailureThreshold)
    36	    }
    37	
    38	    func delay(forAttempt attempt: Int) -> TimeInterval {
    39	        backoffSchedule[min(max(0, attempt - 1), backoffSchedule.count - 1)]
    40	    }
    41	
    42	    static func fromEnvironment(_ environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment) -> Self {
    43	        let schedule = environment["BOSS_ENGINE_RESTART_BACKOFF_SECONDS"]?
    44	            .split(separator: ",")
    45	            .compactMap { TimeInterval($0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)) }
    46	            .filter { $0 > 0 && $0.isFinite }
    47	        let attempts = environment["BOSS_ENGINE_RESTART_MAX_ATTEMPTS"].flatMap(Int.init)
    48	        return Self(
    49	            backoffSchedule: schedule ?? [],
    50	            maximumAttempts: attempts.map { max(1, $0) } ?? Self.default.maximumAttempts
    51	        )
    52	    }
    53	}

   139	            throw error
   140	        }

   143	    private func start(resetRestartBudget: Bool) throws {
   144	        let socketPath = paths.socketPath
   145	        try withStartLock {
   146	            if forceRestart, let running = discoverRunningEngine() {
   147	                emit("[engine restart] terminating existing engine \(describe(running))")
   148	                try stopRunningEngine(running)
   149	            }
   150	
   151	            if let running = discoverRunningEngine() {
   152	                // An engine is already running. Check if its binary matches
   153	                // the app's bundled engine. If not, replace it so the user
   154	                // always gets the version that shipped with this app launch.
   155	                //
   156	                // Each branch emits a distinct log line so a user reporting
   157	                // "engine wasn't restarted after I updated Boss" can grep
   158	                // the system messages and tell exactly which path fired:
   159	                //   [engine version-check skipped: <reason>] — check didn't run
   160	                //   [engine version-check ok] — ran, fingerprints matched
   161	                //   [engine upgrade] — ran, fingerprints differed, restarting
   162	                //
   163	                // BOSS_ENGINE_CMD wins unconditionally (see
   164	                // resolveEngineCommand): a dev running against a custom
   165	                // engine binary has nothing bundled to compare it to, and
   166	                // fingerprinting the *bundled* binary against it would
   167	                // always mismatch and tear down the dev's own engine.
   168	                if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["BOSS_ENGINE_CMD"] != nil {
   169	                    emit("[engine version-check skipped: BOSS_ENGINE_CMD is set (developer custom engine)] attaching to \(describe(running))")
   170	                    return
   171	                }
   172	                guard let bundledPath = bundledEnginePath() else {
   173	                    emit("[engine version-check skipped: no bundled engine in app resources (dev/bazel-run mode)] attaching to \(describe(running))")
   174	                    return
   175	                }
   176	                guard let bundledFP = computeBinaryFingerprint(path: bundledPath) else {
   177	                    throw controllerError("could not fingerprint bundled engine at \(bundledPath)")
   178	                }
   179	
   180	                // A single missed 3s deadline can mean "the engine is busy",
   181	                // not "the engine is stale" — retry a couple of times before
   182	                // treating non-response as a mismatch, so a slow-but-healthy
   183	                // engine isn't torn down and replaced (and doesn't then hit
   184	                // the SIGTERM/SIGKILL fallback if the follow-on shutdown RPC
   185	                // also times out).
   186	                var runningFP: String?
   187	                var fingerprintAttempts = 0
   188	                let maxFingerprintAttempts = 3
   189	                while fingerprintAttempts < maxFingerprintAttempts {
   190	                    fingerprintAttempts += 1
   191	                    runningFP = socketControl.fingerprint(socketPath: running.socketPath, timeoutSeconds: 3.0)
   192	                    if runningFP != nil { break }
   193	                }
   194	
   195	                guard let runningFP else {
   196	                    emit("[engine version-check inconclusive] running fingerprint unavailable after \(fingerprintAttempts) attempts bundled=\(bundledFP) — keeping reachable \(describe(running))")
   197	                    return
   198	                }
   199	                if bundledFP == runningFP {
   200	                    emit("[engine version-check ok] running=\(runningFP) matches bundled — attaching to \(describe(running))")
   201	                    return
   202	                }
   203	                emit("[engine upgrade] running=\(runningFP) bundled=\(bundledFP) — replacing \(describe(running))")
   204	                try stopRunningEngine(running)
   205	                emit("[engine upgrade] old engine stopped — launching new engine from bundle")
   206	            }
   207	
   208	            let (command, bossBinDir) = resolveEngineCommand(socketPath: socketPath)
   209	
   210	            let pid = try launchEngine(command: command, bossBinDir: bossBinDir, socketPath: socketPath)
   211	            lastLaunchError = nil
   212	            emit("[engine launch] detached pid=\(pid) socket=\(socketPath) \(command)")
   213	        }
   214	        // `disableSupervision()` may be called while a supervised relaunch is
   215	        // waiting on filesystem or socket I/O above. It sets this lock-backed
   216	        // flag without waiting for this queue, so do not reactivate polling
   217	        // after that cancellation has won.
   218	        guard !isSupervisionStopped else { return }
   219	        enableSupervision(resetRestartBudget: resetRestartBudget)
   220	    }

   224	    /// Path to the engine binary shipped inside the current app bundle.
   225	    /// Returns `nil` in dev/bazel-run mode where no bundle engine exists.
   226	    private func bundledEnginePath() -> String? {
   227	        if let bundledEnginePathOverride {
   228	            return bundledEnginePathOverride
   229	        }
   230	        guard let resourcePath = Bundle.main.resourcePath else { return nil }
   231	        let path = "\(resourcePath)/bin/\(BossEngineBinary.executableName)"
   232	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: path) else { return nil }

   234	    }

   236	    /// Compute a binary fingerprint of `path` using the same algorithm
   237	    /// as `boss_engine::build_info::binary_fingerprint`:
   238	    ///   SHA-256 of up to 64 MiB of file content → first 6 bytes as
   239	    ///   12 lowercase hex digits, optionally suffixed "-truncated".
   240	    private func computeBinaryFingerprint(path: String) -> String? {
   241	        guard let fh = FileHandle(forReadingAtPath: path) else { return nil }
   242	        defer { try? fh.close() }
   243	
   244	        let cap: Int = 64 * 1024 * 1024
   245	        var hasher = SHA256()
   246	        var readTotal = 0
   247	        var truncated = false
   248	        let chunkSize = 64 * 1024
   249	
   250	        while true {
   251	            let remaining = cap - readTotal
   252	            guard remaining > 0 else {
   253	                // Probe for more bytes to set the truncated flag.
   254	                let probe = (try? fh.read(upToCount: 1)) ?? Data()
   255	                if !probe.isEmpty { truncated = true }
   256	                break
   257	            }
   258	            let toRead = min(chunkSize, remaining)
   259	            guard let chunk = try? fh.read(upToCount: toRead), !chunk.isEmpty else { break }
   260	            hasher.update(data: chunk)
   261	            readTotal += chunk.count
   262	            if chunk.count < toRead {
   263	                // EOF before cap.
   264	                break
   265	            }
   266	        }
   267	
   268	        let digest = hasher.finalize()
   269	        let firstSixBytes = digest.prefix(6)
   270	        let hex = firstSixBytes.map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined()
   271	        return truncated ? "\(hex)-truncated" : hex
   272	    }

   274	    /// Resolve the engine command and the BOSS_BIN_DIR to export.
   275	    ///
   276	    /// Resolution order (per design doc Q3):
   277	    ///   1. BOSS_ENGINE_CMD env override — wins unconditionally so a dev
   278	    ///      running `bazel run //tools/boss/app-macos:Boss` against a custom
   279	    ///      engine still works.
   280	    ///   2. Bundle-relative path: `<Bundle.main.resourcePath>/bin/<engine>` —

   283	    ///   3. `bazel run` fallback — dev mode for when the bundle lacks the
   284	    ///      pre-built engine (e.g. iterating on just the Swift side).
   285	    private func resolveEngineCommand(socketPath: String) -> (command: String, bossBinDir: String?) {
   286	        if let override = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["BOSS_ENGINE_CMD"] {
   287	            return (override, nil)
   288	        }
   289	        if let resourcePath = Bundle.main.resourcePath {
   290	            let enginePath = "\(resourcePath)/bin/\(BossEngineBinary.executableName)"
   291	            if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: enginePath) {
   292	                let bossBinDir = "\(resourcePath)/bin"
   293	                return ("\(shellQuote(enginePath)) --socket-path \(shellQuote(socketPath))", bossBinDir)
   294	            }
   295	        }
   296	        return ("\(BossEngineBinary.bazelRunCommand) -- --socket-path \(shellQuote(socketPath))", nil)
   297	    }

   351	
   352	    /// The engine is deliberately detached from the app so it survives an app
   353	    /// restart. That also means `Process.terminationHandler` cannot observe
   354	    /// it. Polling socket reachability gives the controller the same answer
   355	    /// without making the engine an app child, and serializing this work
   356	    /// prevents two timer ticks from launching competing replacements.
   357	    private func enableSupervision(resetRestartBudget: Bool) {
   358	        // Set this before hopping onto the supervision queue so a later
   359	        // `stop()` always wins, even if this queued block has not run yet.
   360	        setSupervisionStopped(false)
   361	        supervisionQueue.async { [weak self] in
   362	            guard let self else { return }
   363	            if resetRestartBudget {
   364	                self.supervisor.reset()
   365	            }
   366	            if self.supervisionTimer == nil {
   367	                let timer = DispatchSource.makeTimerSource(queue: self.supervisionQueue)
   368	                timer.schedule(
   369	                    deadline: .now() + self.restartPolicy.pollInterval,
   370	                    repeating: self.restartPolicy.pollInterval
   371	                )
   372	                timer.setEventHandler { [weak self] in
   373	                    self?.checkEngineLiveness()
   374	                }
   375	                self.supervisionTimer = timer
   376	                timer.resume()
   377	            }
   378	            self.emitSupervisionState(.running)
   379	        }
   380	    }

   382	    private func disableSupervision() {
   383	        setSupervisionStopped(true)
   384	        supervisionQueue.async { [weak self] in
   385	            guard let self else { return }
   386	            pendingRestart?.cancel()
   387	            pendingRestart = nil
   388	            supervisionTimer?.cancel()
   389	            supervisionTimer = nil
   390	        }
   391	    }

   393	    private func checkEngineLiveness() {
   394	        guard !isSupervisionStopped, pendingRestart == nil else { return }
   395	        let liveness: (isReachable: Bool, source: String)
   396	        if let livenessProbe {
   397	            liveness = (livenessProbe(), "engine client connection")
   398	        } else {
   399	            liveness = (discoverRunningEngine() != nil, "socket probe")
   400	        }
   401	        let action = supervisor.tick(isAlive: liveness.isReachable, now: Date())
   402	        switch action {
   403	        case .running:
   404	            lastLaunchError = nil
   405	            emitSupervisionState(.running)
   406	            return
   407	        case let .unreachable(consecutiveFailures, requiredFailures):
   408	            emit("[engine supervision] \(liveness.source) reported engine unreachable; failed liveness tick \(consecutiveFailures)/\(requiredFailures), keeping engine running")
   409	            return
   410	        case let .gaveUp(attempts):
   411	            emit("[engine supervision] gave up after \(attempts) restart attempts; use Restart engine to try again")
   412	            emitSupervisionState(.gaveUp(attempts: attempts, lastError: lastLaunchError))
   413	            return
   414	        case let .restart(attempt, delay):
   415	            emit("[engine supervision] engine remained unreachable for \(restartPolicy.consecutiveFailureThreshold) consecutive ticks; restart attempt \(attempt)/\(restartPolicy.maximumAttempts) in \(Int(delay))s")
   416	            emitSupervisionState(.restarting(attempt: attempt, retryAfter: delay))
   417	            let work = DispatchWorkItem { [weak self] in
   418	                self?.relaunchAfterUnexpectedExit(attempt: attempt)
   419	            }
   420	            pendingRestart = work
   421	            supervisionQueue.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + delay, execute: work)
   422	        case .wait:
   423	            return
   424	        }
   425	    }
   426	
   427	    private func relaunchAfterUnexpectedExit(attempt: Int) {
   428	        pendingRestart = nil
   429	        guard !isSupervisionStopped else { return }
   430	        do {
   431	            try start(resetRestartBudget: false)
   432	        } catch {
   433	            lastLaunchError = error.localizedDescription
   434	            emit("[engine supervision] restart launch failed: \(error.localizedDescription)")
   435	            emitSupervisionState(.restartFailed(attempt: attempt, message: error.localizedDescription))
   436	            // The next timer tick applies the next backoff slot.
   437	        }
   438	    }

   440	    private func launchEngine(command: String, bossBinDir: String?, socketPath: String) throws -> pid_t {
   441	        if let launchHandler {
   442	            return try launchHandler(command, bossBinDir, socketPath)
   443	        }
   444	        return try launchDetached(command: command, bossBinDir: bossBinDir, socketPath: socketPath)

   447	    private func launchDetached(command: String, bossBinDir: String?, socketPath: String) throws -> pid_t {
   448	        let launchErrorPath = URL(fileURLWithPath: paths.pidPath)
   449	            .deletingLastPathComponent()
   450	            .appendingPathComponent("engine-launch.log")
   451	            .path
   452	        let proc = Process()
   453	        proc.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/bin/zsh")
   454	        // zsh's BG_NICE option (on by default) reduces the priority of any
   455	        // job started with `&` by a non-interactive shell — nice(5) rather
   456	        // than the caller's own nice(0) — because a `zsh -c` script has no
   457	        // job control (monitor mode) active. That silently demoted the
   458	        // detached engine, and everything it forks (the private tmux
   459	        // server, then the coordinator's `claude` pane inside it) inherit
   460	        // that nice(5) by plain fork inheritance. `NO_BG_NICE` keeps the
   461	        // backgrounded engine at the same priority as this app.
   462	        //
   463	        // This only reaches a tmux server started by a post-fix engine: a
   464	        // private server already running under the durable state-root socket
   465	        // is never killed by this codebase, so on an existing install it
   466	        // keeps the nice(5) it was born with even after this fix ships. After
   467	        // upgrading, `tmux -S "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Boss/tmux.sock"
   468	        // kill-server` (or a reboot) once so the next engine launch creates a
   469	        // fresh server under this corrected priority. A leftover `-L boss`
   470	        // server is drained at boot rather than relocated.
   471	        let script = """
   472	        setopt NO_BG_NICE
   473	        : > \(shellQuote(launchErrorPath))
   474	        nohup \(command) >/dev/null 2>\(shellQuote(launchErrorPath)) &
   475	        child=$!
   476	        print -r -- $child
   477	        sleep 0.25
   478	        if ! kill -0 $child 2>/dev/null; then
   479	          wait $child
   480	          exit $?
   481	        fi
   482	        """
   483	        proc.arguments = ["-c", script]
   484	        proc.currentDirectoryURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: launchDirectory, isDirectory: true)
   485	        // Tell the engine the app's pid explicitly. `bazel run`
   486	        // daemonizes its server, which reparents the engine binary
   487	        // away from the app's process tree, so `getppid()` and any
   488	        // ancestor walk both miss the real app. The engine reads
   489	        // BOSS_APP_PID to set its trust root for `RegisterAppSession`.
   490	        var env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
   491	        env["BOSS_APP_PID"] = String(getpid())
   492	        // The engine's tracing layer continues writing its bounded text log,
   493	        // while direct startup failures from Rust's main function land in the
   494	        // launch-error file above for this controller to surface verbatim.
   495	        env["BOSS_ENGINE_STDERR_LOGGING"] = "0"
   496	        // BOSS_BIN_DIR tells the engine where its sibling CLIs live
   497	        // (boss, bossctl, boss-event) in installed mode. The engine
   498	        // propagates this to workers so they resolve the bundled copies
   499	        // rather than any PATH match. Unset in dev mode (no bundle bin/).
   500	        if let dir = bossBinDir {
   501	            env["BOSS_BIN_DIR"] = dir
   502	        }
   503	        // When launched from Finder/Dock/launchctl, the app inherits a minimal
   504	        // launchd GUI session PATH (/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin) that omits
   505	        // developer tool directories. The engine and its cube subprocesses need
   506	        // jj, mint, and other tools that live outside that minimal set.
   507	        //
   508	        // We prepend well-known locations rather than shelling out to read the
   509	        // user's login-shell PATH (which would be more accurate but brittle — a
   510	        // misbehaving shell init could hang the app or print garbage). Extra
   511	        // segments that don't exist on a given machine are ignored by the kernel.
   512	        env["PATH"] = augmentedPATH(current: env["PATH"] ?? "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin")
   513	        // If the user pasted an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY into Settings → Engine,
   514	        // override whatever the launchd parent inherited so the Settings
   515	        // value always wins (work item #735). When no Settings value is
   516	        // stored, leave the inherited env entry untouched so a shell
   517	        // `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=…` followed by `boss` from a terminal
   518	        // continues to work for users who prefer that path.
   519	        if let stored = APIKeyStore.readAnthropicApiKey() {
   520	            env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] = stored
   521	        }
   522	        proc.environment = env
   523	        let output = Pipe()
   524	        let shellError = Pipe()
   525	        proc.standardOutput = output
   526	        proc.standardError = shellError
   527	
   528	        try proc.run()
   529	        proc.waitUntilExit()
   530	        let outputData = output.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()
   531	        let shellErrorData = shellError.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()
   532	        let childPID = String(data: outputData, encoding: .utf8)?
   533	            .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
   534	            .split(separator: "\n")
   535	            .first
   536	            .flatMap { pid_t($0) }
   537	        if proc.terminationStatus != 0 {
   538	            let shellMessage = String(data: shellErrorData, encoding: .utf8)?
   539	                .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
   540	            throw controllerError(
   541	                launchFailureMessage(
   542	                    prefix: "engine process exited during launch with status \(proc.terminationStatus)",
   543	                    launchErrorPath: launchErrorPath,
   544	                    fallback: shellMessage
   545	                ),
   546	                code: Int(proc.terminationStatus)
   547	            )
   548	        }
   549	        guard let childPID, childPID > 1 else {
   550	            throw controllerError("detached engine launcher did not report the child pid")
   551	        }
   552	
   553	        // The frontend socket binds late in engine startup — after
   554	        // `WorkDb::open`, the tmux preflight probe (which shells out to
   555	        // tmux), and planner-run recovery — so a slow-but-healthy start can
   556	        // legitimately outlast this window, especially the `bazel run`
   557	        // command shape used in dev mode, where a cold build alone can
   558	        // exceed it. Only the child actually exiting (checked every
   559	        // iteration above) is treated as a launch failure; a still-running
   560	        // child that simply hasn't bound its socket yet is not killed —
   561	        // supervision (`checkEngineLiveness`) observes the outcome once the
   562	        // socket comes up, or once the process actually exits.
   563	        let readinessWindow: TimeInterval = command.contains(BossEngineBinary.bazelRunCommand) ? 120 : 30
   564	        let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(readinessWindow)
   565	        while Date() < deadline {
   566	            if socketControl.isReachable(socketPath: socketPath, timeoutSeconds: 0.5) {
   567	                return childPID
   568	            }
   569	            if !isProcessRunning(childPID) {
   570	                throw controllerError(
   571	                    launchFailureMessage(
   572	                        prefix: "engine process pid=\(childPID) exited before its socket became reachable",
   573	                        launchErrorPath: launchErrorPath,
   574	                        fallback: nil
   575	                    )
   576	                )
   577	            }
   578	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.1)
   579	        }
   580	
   581	        emit(
   582	            "[engine launch] pid=\(childPID) socket \(socketPath) not yet reachable after \(Int(readinessWindow))s; still running, leaving it to supervision rather than killing it"
   583	        )
   584	        return childPID
   585	    }

   587	    private func launchFailureMessage(prefix: String, launchErrorPath: String, fallback: String?) -> String {
   588	        let data = try? Data(contentsOf: URL(fileURLWithPath: launchErrorPath))
   589	        let tail = data.map { Data($0.suffix(32 * 1024)) }
   590	        let engineError = tail.flatMap { String(data: $0, encoding: .utf8) }?
   591	            .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
   592	        let detail = [engineError, fallback]
   593	            .compactMap { $0 }
   594	            .first { !$0.isEmpty }
   595	        return detail.map { "\(prefix): \($0)" } ?? prefix
   596	    }

   602	    /// Prepend standard developer-tool directories to PATH so the engine and its
   603	    /// subprocesses (cube, jj, mint, cargo binaries) can be found when the app is
   604	    /// launched from Finder/Dock/launchctl with a minimal launchd PATH.
   605	    ///
   606	    /// Order matches typical shell precedence: Apple Silicon Homebrew, Intel/manual
   607	    /// Homebrew, LinkedIn corporate tools, Rust/Cargo, then user-local directories.
   608	    /// Segments that don't exist on the current machine are harmless — the kernel
   609	    /// skips non-existent PATH entries. The original launchd PATH is preserved at the
   610	    /// end so system tools continue to resolve normally.
   611	    private func augmentedPATH(current: String) -> String {
   612	        let home = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["HOME"] ?? NSHomeDirectory()
   613	        let extra = [
   614	            "/opt/homebrew/bin",        // Apple Silicon Homebrew (jj, etc.)
   615	            "/usr/local/bin",           // Intel Homebrew, manual installs
   616	            "/usr/local/linkedin/bin",  // LinkedIn corporate tools (mint, etc.)
   617	            "\(home)/.cargo/bin",       // Rust binaries (jj commonly installed here)
   618	            "\(home)/bin",              // user-local binaries
   619	            "\(home)/.local/bin",       // XDG-style user-local binaries
   620	        ]
   621	        // Deduplicate: keep the first occurrence of each segment.
   622	        var seen = Set(current.split(separator: ":").map(String.init))
   623	        let unique = extra.filter { seen.insert($0).inserted }
   624	        let prefix = unique.joined(separator: ":")
   625	        return prefix.isEmpty ? current : "\(prefix):\(current)"
   626	    }

   628	    private func discoverRunningEngine() -> RunningEngine? {
   629	        for endpoint in paths.endpointPaths {
   630	            guard socketControl.isReachable(socketPath: endpoint.socketPath) else {
   631	                continue
   632	            }
   633	            // Peer credentials are direct, unforgeable proof of which
   634	            // process owns the socket we just connected to; the pid file is
   635	            // the deletable, potentially stale artefact this discovery step
   636	            // otherwise leans on. Prefer the peer pid and only fall back to
   637	            // the file when peer credentials aren't available.
   638	            let pid = socketControl.peerPID(socketPath: endpoint.socketPath, timeoutSeconds: 1)
   639	                ?? currentEnginePID(pidPath: endpoint.pidPath)

/bin/zsh -lc '"$BOSS_BIN" propose review-guide --body '"'# PR #2886: Preserve reachable engines when checks are inconclusive

## Orientation

Boss should keep using a reachable background engine when a build check cannot produce an answer, avoiding an unnecessary replacement. The engine is the separate process that the Boss macOS app connects to; it can remain running across app launches. This bug fix changes the app component responsible for starting, reusing, and recovering that process.

Previously, an unanswered build check could cause Boss to stop the existing engine and launch another. Now, an unavailable answer preserves the discovered engine; a confirmed build mismatch still triggers replacement. During ongoing monitoring, Boss also waits for three consecutive unreachable checks before scheduling recovery, instead of reacting to the first failed check.

A **fingerprint** is a short identifier derived from the engine executable, used to compare the running engine with the copy shipped in the app. An **RPC** is a request sent to the engine for a response. **Supervision** is periodic reachability monitoring; each check is a **tick**, and **backoff** is the delay before a recovery attempt.

## Change overview

The change separates two kinds of evidence:

- **Build identity:** three unsuccessful fingerprint requests mean “inconclusive,” while an actual unequal fingerprint means “replace.”
- **Reachability:** one or two failed supervision ticks mean “keep waiting,” while the third consecutive failure permits a recovery attempt.

The [startup decision](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L186-L205) preserves the existing three attempts, each with a three-second timeout. The [restart policy](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L9-L35) adds a default consecutive-failure threshold of three, clamped to at least one. Its existing one-second polling interval, six-attempt budget, delay schedule, and 60-second healthy-reset interval remain.

## Core implementation

The existing division of responsibilities remains: "'`EngineProcessController` discovers and launches processes, while `EngineSupervisor` makes recovery decisions from reachability observations and retry history. The supervisor adds a failure counter and an `.unreachable(consecutiveFailures:requiredFailures:)` action; the controller handles that action by logging and returning without scheduling recovery.

The normal app caller [starts the controller before starting its engine client](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/ChatViewModel.swift#L1957-L1977). It also [supplies the existing client connection as the supervision signal](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/ChatViewModel.swift#L1215-L1228). That signal becomes true when the connection is ready and false on waiting, failure, or cancellation ([connection transitions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineClient.swift#L107-L139)). Without an injected signal, the controller discovers an engine through a fresh local socket connection—a socket is the local communication endpoint between the app and engine.

## Implementation walkthrough

### 1. Keep “unknown build” separate from “different build”

[Discovery](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L628-L646) first establishes that an endpoint accepts a connection. The subsequent [fingerprint helper](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/BossEnginePaths.swift#L280-L291) returns an optional string: an unsuccessful request, unexpected response type, or absent string fingerprint yields `nil`.

At the merge base, [both missing and unequal fingerprints reached the stop-and-replace path](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L186-L204). The new guard returns when the fingerprint remains unavailable. The resulting decision is:

```text
Condensed pseudocode:
request running fingerprint up to three times
if no fingerprint:
    log inconclusive; keep discovered engine
else if running fingerprint equals bundled fingerprint:
    keep discovered engine
else:
    stop existing engine; launch replacement
```

The [actual branch and launch continuation](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L186-L219) matter together: the early return exits the start-lock closure, so the outer method still enables supervision. It skips replacement, not ongoing monitoring.

This contract applies after discovery and the normal version-check prerequisites. [Forced restart, a custom engine command, absence of a bundled executable, and failure to fingerprint that executable](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L143-L178) retain their existing branches.

### 2. Worked example: reachable engine, unanswered fingerprint requests

The [new regression test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L224-L238) provides a concrete input: the primary endpoint is reachable, the fixture supplies a bundled executable, and `fingerprintAvailable: false` makes every fingerprint request return `nil`. The [fixture](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L373-L403) disables forced restart and records launch requests.

1. Discovery finds the reachable endpoint.
2. Both versions request its fingerprint three times without obtaining a value.
3. Previously, execution fell through to `stopRunningEngine` and then replacement launch.
4. Now, the missing-value guard logs an inconclusive check and returns from the closure. The observable test result is three fingerprint requests, **zero shutdown requests, and zero launches**.

The contrasting boundary is a positive mismatch: the [existing stale-engine test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L209-L222) supplies `"stale-engine"` and still expects shutdown of the older endpoint and replacement launch on the primary endpoint.

### 3. Require consecutive failures before spending a recovery attempt

Previously, [one failed tick immediately advanced the restart budget](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift#L43-L54). Now, after incrementing the failure counter and checking whether the budget is exhausted, the supervisor applies this gate:

```swift
guard consecutiveFailures >= policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold else {
    return .unreachable(
        consecutiveFailures: consecutiveFailures,
        requiredFailures: policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    )
}
consecutiveFailures = 0
```

[Source](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift#L47-L65). Only after this gate does it increment the attempt count or report that the budget has run out. A reachable tick immediately clears the failure streak; replenishing the retry budget still requires the configured healthy interval. An explicit reset clears both counters ([reset and healthy handling](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift#L25-L44)).

With the default threshold, failed observations produce `unreachable(1, 3)`, `unreachable(2, 3)`, then `restart(attempt: 1, delay: 1)`. An intervening reachable observation starts the streak over. This is a count of observations, rather than an elapsed-time test.

### 4. Turn the decision into recovery and diagnostic output

The [controller action handler](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L393-L438) logs the signal source—“engine client connection” or “socket probe”—and failure count for deferred recovery. At the threshold, the message reports consecutive unreachability instead of claiming the process exited, then emits the restarting state and schedules the existing delayed work.

Ticks are skipped while a restart is pending. When the delay expires, recovery calls `start(resetRestartBudget: false)`, preserving the attempt budget and reusing the same discovery/version-check rules. Scheduling recovery therefore does not itself guarantee that a process will be replaced. Output continues through the [existing system-message callback](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/ChatViewModel.swift#L1275-L1281).
